questions.question:
Your product's nearest competitor has lower market share, but has higher customer satisfaction, though they lack some key features of your product. You are losing market share to them as customers discover them. They release 3 times faster than you, which is helping them to win customers. What should you do first in response?

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Lower your product's price to make it more attractive to new and existing customers.
Find new markets for your product that your competitor is not yet in.
Improve your time-to-market and rate of innovation to improve your responsiveness.
Add features to your next release that you think will retain and win customers.

questions.question:
The Developers have struggled to get all of their forecasted work done during the last three Sprints. As a Product Owner what steps could you take to help the Developers improve their ability to deliver a done Increment?

(choose the best two answers)

options.text: Add more people to the team so they can get more done.
The Product Owner can spend more time with the Developers.
Ask the Scrum Master to help the Developers learn techniques for improving their ability to forecast work.
Ensure that all Developers are top performers.

questions.question:
What is a benefit of frequent product releases?

(choose the best answer)

options.text: They enable teams to inspect and adapt more frequently.
They help teams better understand and meet customer needs.
They help teams to learn how to correct and eliminate errors.
Smaller, more frequent releases are less risky.
All of the above.
None of the above.

questions.question:
Personas can help to:

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Understand the needs of a set of users.
Formulate hypotheses about product value.
Understand market potential.
Discover key buying triggers.
All of the above.

questions.question:
You are the Product Owner for a product with diverse stakeholders with differing opinions that sometimes conflict.

Your Director of Marketing strongly believes that you should add a major new feature to reach a new market. Your CEO believes that the new feature is too expensive and thinks you should focus on other features to make existing customers happier. The CEO says that as Product Owner it is ultimately your decision.

You think both perspectives have merit, but you cannot do both. How should you proceed?

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Trust the CEO's opinion and focus on current customers, since you cannot afford unhappy customers.
Trust the Director of Marketing's opinion and add the features; when revenues increase, you will be vindicated.
Devise an experiment that will help the company to better understand the new market and its potential.
Better understand the positions of other stakeholders to gather more information, then make a decision.

questions.question:
When should the Product Owner update the project plan?

(choose the best answer)

options.text: The Product Backlog is the plan in Scrum. It is updated as new information and insights emerge.
The project plan must be updated prior to the Sprint Retrospective.
Before the Sprint Planning to know how much work will have to be done in the Sprint.
After the Daily Scrum to ensure an accurate daily overview of project progress.

questions.question:
Given only the information in the following three statements:
- Product A has a greater potential market than Product B.
- Product A has lower customer satisfaction than Product B.
- Product B produces more revenue at the present time.

Which investment strategies should you consider for these two products?

(choose the best answer)

options.text: For both products, continually measure the impact of any new investments or marketing.
Invest in Product A to increase its market share, customer satisfaction, and revenue.
Investigate an increase in marketing for Product B to grow its market share.
All of the above.

questions.question:
Choose the statement that best describes who is accountable for engaging the stakeholders to ensure value is delivered.

(choose the best answer)

options.text: The Product Owner is responsible, but engagement can be delegated.
The project manager schedules all stakeholder interactions.
The team manager is responsible for managing the time spent with stakeholders.
The Developers are responsible for all stakeholder engagement.
The business analyst since they are the Subject Matter Expert.

questions.question:
Which of the following are characteristics of a Product Goal?

(choose all that apply)

options.text: It forms a contract with the business, allowing change to be better managed.
It enhances focus.
It communicates the target future state of the product.
It has the approval of all stakeholders.
It provides a long-term objective for the Scrum Team to plan against.
It is a commitment contained in the Product Backlog.

questions.question:
The smallest product Increment that is valuable enough to release is one that:

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Delivers a single new or improved outcome.
Adds a new feature.
Fixes at least one defect.
Delivers all "must do" Product Backlog items.

questions.question:
The primary accountability of a Product Owner is:

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Writing User Stories that the Scrum Team can fully understand.
Maximizing the value of the work that the Scrum Team delivers.
Interfacing between the Developers and the customers.
Managing the Product Backlog.

questions.question:
In order to justify the price increase of a product, your primary objective should be to:

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Reduce the price for a period of time before increasing it above the original price.
Reduce the number of features to make the product easier to use.
Improve the value experienced by the customer.
Add more features to make the product more attractive.

questions.question:
When the Product Owner is too busy to work with all of the teams in a multi-team product development effort, which strategy will help them?

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Add component team Product Owners.
Communicate a clear Product Goal and delegate some activities to the Developers.
Enlist the Program Management Office to help coordinate work.
Assign sub-Product Owners to each Scrum Team.
All of the above.

questions.question:
Which of the following are true about the length of the Sprint?

(choose all that apply)

options.text: Sprint length is determined during Sprint Planning and should be long enough to make sure the Developers can deliver what is to be accomplished in the upcoming Sprint.
All Sprints must be 1 month or less.
It is best to have Sprints of consistent length.
Sprint length is determined during Sprint Planning and should hold the time it will take to create the planned features in the upcoming Sprint, but does not include time for any validation.
The length of the Sprint should be proportional to the work that is done in between Sprints.

questions.question:
As an investor or shareholder, which of the following measures might give you insight about whether a product is delivering value?

(choose all that apply)

options.text: Revenue per Employee.
Market Share.
The average selling price as compared to close competitors.
Product profitability.
The weekly velocity of the Developers.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about the Product Backlog are true?

(choose the best two answers)

options.text: All Product Backlog Items must be expressed as user stories.
The Product Backlog should be visible to the Scrum Team and stakeholders.
Only the Product Owner can place items on the Product Backlog.
All Product Backlog items for the current Sprint and the next Sprint must be identified before the Sprint begins in case the Developer's velocity exceeds the selected Product Backlog items.
The Product Backlog represents the input of all stakeholders and eliminates any need for the Developers to speak to stakeholders.
The Product Backlog is ordered by the Product Owner.

questions.question:
Sharing people with unique skills across multiple teams will likely result in which of the following conditions?

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Teams may wait more often, impeding the delivery of value.
Costs are lower since expensive resources are shared.
Teams do not have to develop deep technical skills.
More work gets done since people are better utilized.

questions.question:
Who determines when it is appropriate to update the Sprint Backlog during a Sprint?

(choose the best answer)

options.text: The Project Manager.
The Scrum Team.
The Developers.
The Product Owner.

questions.question:
A Product Owner is needed for every:

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Product.
Portfolio.
Program.
All of the above.

questions.question:
A user satisfaction gap exists when there is a difference between:

(choose the best two answers)

options.text: The user's actual experience.
The user's desired outcome.
The total market size.
The market share of the product.

questions.question:
You are a Product Owner for a product with a rapidly declining customer base.

Despite data that indicates the decline is due to a shrinking market, rather than a lack of new features, an influential stakeholder insists on adding more features to attract new customers. The influential stakeholder also says that if you do not add new features you risk losing your most profitable customer.

Which two of the following actions might you take?

(choose the best two answers)

options.text: Acknowledge the views of the influential stakeholder but decline to add more features to the product.
Collaborate with other stakeholders and use a voting system to decide which options should be considered.
Agree with the stakeholder and add features to the Product Backlog as it might increase your customer base.
Collaborate with the stakeholder to run a small experiment to validate their opinion.

questions.question:
What are the attributes of a good Product Vision and Strategy?

(choose all that apply)

options.text: It describes what value means in the context of the product, and how it can be measured.
It describes who will use the product and what they would like to achieve.
It describes how the product compares to competitor products.
It describes how people will use the product to achieve potential outcomes.

questions.question:
A separate Product Backlog is needed for every:

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Product.
Scrum Team.
Portfolio.
Program.
All of the above.

questions.question:
Who is responsible for the sizing of Product Backlog items?

(choose the best answer)

options.text: The Developers, alone.
The Scrum Master.
The Product Owner with input from the Developers.
The Developers after clarifying requirements with the Product Owner.
The most senior people in the organization, including architects and subject matter experts.

questions.question:
The most important thing a Product Owner can do is:

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Function as the single source of truth for all requirements.
Ensure that all stakeholder needs are met.
Maximize the value delivered by the product.
Determine the release schedule and contents.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is true about the Product Vision?

(choose the best answer)

options.text: It evolves as the Scrum Team learns more about customers and their needs.
It is the shared responsibility of the Scrum Team to develop and evolve.
It must be completely free from discussions about strategic technology choices.
All of the above.
None of the above.

questions.question:
You started measuring product feature usage in your last release. You are surprised to learn that a sizable percentage of the features you thought were very important are never or rarely used.

Which of the following actions could you take to further evaluate this unexpected result?

(choose all that apply)

options.text: Spend more time talking to users to identify the impact they seek.
Disable the features that have never been used and listen for feedback.
Run experiments to increase your understanding of what customers find valuable.
Examine whether the rarely used features solve the intended problem.

questions.question:
The Developers inform the Product Owner during the Sprint that they are not likely to complete everything they forecasted. What would you expect a Product Owner to do?

(choose the best answer)

options.text: End the Sprint, since the goal cannot be achieved.
Skip Product Backlog refinement activities.
Change the Sprint Goal to match what the Developers can deliver.
Reduce the scope of the Sprint, if possible, to still meet the Sprint Goal.
Inform management that more resources are needed.

questions.question:
Which of the following practices might help the Product Owner minimize waste in developing and sustaining the Product Backlog?

(choose all that apply)

options.text: Only fully describe the Product Backlog items near the top of the Product Backlog since they are more likely to be selected during Sprint Planning.
Maintain newly gathered Product Backlog items in a separate Product Backlog until they are fully understood to avoid distracting the Developers.
Write Product Backlog items with clearly expressed expected outcomes.
As Product Owner, ask the Developers to refine several important Product Backlog items.

questions.question:
A Sprint forecast is:

(choose the best answer)

options.text: A useful tool for management to understand team performance and capacity.
A commitment the Developers makes to deliver a particular set of Product Backlog items.
The amount of work the Developers believe they can complete in that Sprint.
Useful for the stakeholders to know what will be included in future releases.

questions.question:
An effective Product Owner must:

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Ensure that every stakeholder need is met.
Be the "expert" opinion for all Product Backlog items.
Ensure that the team is as productive as possible.
Be the single point of contact for all stakeholders.
All of the above.
None of the above.

questions.question:
You are the Product Owner at a small company with a single product. You have authority over pricing, promotion, and how much is invested in new features or capabilities. Your product has:
- High Current Value - as indicated by high customer satisfaction.
- High Unrealized Value - as indicated by low market share.

Using those two data points, what is the first action you should take to increase the business performance of the product?

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Release an identical product to market, but give it a new product name.
Drop the price of the product to attract a greater number of customers.
Increase the number of product features to attract a greater number of customers.
Improve the marketing of the product to attract a greater number of customers.

questions.question:
Managing a Product Backlog involves which of the following activities?

(choose all that apply)

options.text: Forecasting the effort of Product Backlog items.
Ordering the Product Backlog.
Breaking large Product Backlog items into multiple smaller Product Backlog items.
Reducing or eliminating dependencies between Product Backlog items.
Reviewing the Product Backlog with stakeholders.

questions.question:
As a Product Owner you become aware that the quality assurance criteria, defined in the Definition of Done, were not met for the latest Increment. Which of the following statements are true?

(choose the best four answers)

options.text: The project manager cannot effectively update the plan.
The incomplete Sprint Backlog items should be returned to the Product Backlog.
The indication of progress on the Product Backlog is not transparent.
The next Sprint may be interrupted when quality issues are encountered.
The Scrum Team should not release the Increment.

questions.question:
Which of the following might the Scrum Team discuss during a Sprint Retrospective?

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Methods of communication.
The way the Scrum Team does Sprint Planning.
Skills needed to improve the Scrum Team's ability to deliver.
Its Definition of Done.
All of the above.

questions.question:
Product A is a big revenue producer; it has:
- High Current Value and Low Unrealized Value.

Product B is a new product with a lot of potential; it has:
- Low Current Value and High Unrealized Value.

Using those two data points and taking a long-term view, which of the options below should you pursue?

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Weight your investment toward Product A; you do not want to risk losing customers.
Weight your investment toward Product B; since it has more potential.
Invest equally in both products.

questions.question:
Which of the following activities should a Product Owner never do?

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Establish a Product Goal.
Dictate the Sprint Goal.
Decide when to release the product Increment.
Accept work done during the Sprint.

questions.question:
You have been a Product Owner at a new company for a few weeks. It has become clear to you that many people, both inside and outside the Scrum Team, expect close involvement in the decisions that you, as a Product Owner, are accountable for.

As a result, you find that it takes too long to make decisions. Which of the following are reasonable options you could take?

(choose the best three answers)

options.text: Create and share a delegation board that displays your decision-making areas and work with your Scrum Team to clarify decision making accountability and responsibility.
Allow other members of the Scrum Team and stakeholders to continue making decisions they are not accountable for; documenting which decisions do not deliver the intended value.
Demonstrate, with the help of data, how long it is taking you to make decisions and the impact that the long decision-making cycle has on delivering value to the customer.
Work with your Scrum Master to better understand what next steps you can take to move the company's understanding of product ownership up in the maturity curve towards Entrepreneur.
Start making all the decisions without consulting the others who have expressed interest.

questions.question:
If burndown charts are used to visualize progress, what do they track?

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Accumulated cost.
Individual worker productivity.
Work remaining across time.
Accumulated business value delivered to the customer.

questions.question:
Your stakeholders are very demanding and each of them has at least one feature that they say is essential for the next release. As the Product Owner, you have validated that the feature requests are all valid requests and would likely add value to your product. What should you do?

(choose the best answer)

options.text: Escalate to the steering committee to make the call.
Wait until all essential features are complete before releasing the product.
Pick the two most influential stakeholders and satisfy their needs, then release.
Release when you can satisfy at least a single outcome, even though not all features are implemented.
